newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila hints extending IMF programme possible.
newsitem.headline: Manila hints extending IMF programme possible.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos suggested on Wednesday an extension of a three-year International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme for the Philippines was a possibility if Congress failed to pass a crucial tax bill before end-June.

"We are just playing it safe by having a fallback position," Ramos told a news conference when asked about earlier statements by the Central Bank that Manila might ask for an extension of the IMF programme.
The Congress has nine days to act on the tax measure before adjourning its present session and reconvening in the third week of July.

The IMF programme, supposed to be the country's last after nearly three decades under IMF supervision, is scheduled to lapse on June 23. The programme calls for reform measures to put the economy on a steady growth path.
The tax bill, the last of the economic reforms called for under the IMF programme, is expected to widen the base of corporate and individual taxpayers and plug loopholes in the income tax system.
Its passage will assure the government of a steady revenue flow in the coming years.
Congressional leaders are debating tax exemption levels as well as the corporate tax rates to be included in the bill.
"Both chambers assured us of the eventual passage of that, if not by the end of June, certainly, they said they will give it highest priority in the next session," Ramos said.
